decisions.reason: The 5V boost rating and load allocation do not change the independently specified DCDC1 3.3V rail, whose same-message introduction already captures its own loads and rating.
Assigning specific loads to the downstream 5V boost does not alter the existing rule that the AXP2101 is the normal-operation power source for all system loads.
The boost converter rating and powered loads do not affect the battery connector family, pin count, pin functions, or unresolved pin order.
The source does not change battery protection circuitry, thresholds, or protection functions.
The source does not change the battery NTC connection or thermal-monitoring behavior.
The 5V boost load allocation does not change the dedicated charge LED circuit or the selected charge-status display method.
The standalone USB supply remains limited to the complete 3.3V rail; its same-message MODIFY already captures the LDO and source-selection rules independently of the 5V boost loads.
The boost rating and downstream sensor allocation do not change the existing 5V power connection or 5V_EN signal pinout.
The power-rail clarification has no effect on the selected four-layer PCB stack.
Allocating sensors to the 5V boost does not add, remove, or reorganize any project board.
The source identifies power rails for particular sensors but does not change the sensor board's connector-fanout role or interfaces.
The source conditionally places SK6812 LEDs on the 5V rail but explicitly says this depends on the LED version, so a definitive power-interface modification requires resolution of that choice.
